summary: This Wikipedia-derived note surveys Richmond, Virginia, covering its political and religious history, motorsports and sports teams, corporate presence, historic churches, monuments, neighborhoods, city government, theater, water and wastewater infrastructure, climate, geography, rail service, and film industry activity. It presents Richmond as the Virginia state capital and the center of the Richmond metropolitan area, with a long mix of colonial, Civil War-era and modern developments.
one_line: Overview of Richmond, Virginia, the state capital, covering its history, religion, politics, sports, churches, monuments, government, climate, geography and film industry.
key_facts: In 1990, Reverend A. Carl Prince was elected to the Richmond City Council from the Eighth District in South Richmond, becoming the first African American Baptist Minister elected to the council.
The Richmond International Raceway has hosted NASCAR Sprint Cup races since 1953.
Southside Speedway, in Chesterfield County, has operated since 1959 and is a .333-mile oval known as the "Toughest Track in the South".
Capital One Financial Corporation is officially based in McLean, Virginia, but was founded in Richmond and has its operations center and most employees in the Richmond area.
UPS Freight, formerly known as Overnite Transportation, has its corporate headquarters in Richmond.
First Baptist Church of Richmond, established in 1780, was the first Baptist church in the city.
Second Presbyterian Church of Richmond was founded on February 5, 1845, and was the first Gothic building and first gas-lit church built in Richmond.
St. Peter's Church was dedicated on May 25, 1834, and became the first Catholic church in Richmond.
Richmond's original street grid was laid out in 1737.
The city's wastewater utility operates 1,500 miles of sanitary sewer and the 44-million-gallon Shockoe Retention Basin.
Richmond's July daily mean temperature is 79.3 °F (26.3 °C), and its extreme temperature range runs from −12 °F on January 19, 1940 to 107 °F on August 6, 1918.
Richmond was incorporated in 1742 and has been an independent city since 1871.
The Richmond Flying Squirrels opened their first season at The Diamond on April 15, 2010.
Richmond city council representatives serve four-year terms, with the council meeting at City Hall on the second and fourth Mondays of each month except August.
The film Lincoln, shot in the Richmond area, led to Daniel Day-Lewis's third Oscar.
